summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars
This project explores the forgotten machines left behind by NASA during its missions to the Moon and Mars. These include lunar landers, rovers, scientific instruments, flags, and other equipment that played important roles in space exploration but were never brought back to Earth.
Rather than viewing these machines as abandoned objects, this project presents them as silent heroes of space exploration. It highlights their remarkable journeys, achievements, challenges, and contributions to science. Special attention is given to the Opportunity rover, which operated for nearly 15 years despite being designed for just 90 days, and the Ingenuity helicopter, which completed 72 flights on Mars despite an original goal of only five.
The project also explores how the extreme environments of the Moon and Mars affect these machines, why they remain on other worlds, and how they continue to serve as historical evidence of human exploration.
Through scientific information, real photographs, and creative storytelling, this project brings these forgotten machines back to life. It reminds us that although their missions have ended, their discoveries and contributions will remain part of human history.
